content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: the no-cost plan (delay Payments breaks, move 2 cross-skilled agents from General, IVR callback) lifts the 14:15-16:15 service level to 88.6% against an 80% target.","why":"A sick wave, mostly 'Unplanned leave - family function', has left Payments at 55 agents vs 62.4 expected and General at 45 vs 57.6. Call volume and handle times are near forecast. Even with no action, the window is predicted at 87.5% (Payments 84.7%), so the target is already met. P1 costs nothing and shores up Payments, the weaker queue, raising it to 87.6%. Abandons ease slightly from 2.5% to 2.4%. No policy issues and no escalation needed.","trade_offs":["General gives up some headroom, falling from 91.1% to 89.8% while 2 agents help Payments. It stays well above 80%.","Rest-of-day service level dips slightly to 90.8% (vs 91.2% with no action).","P3 does best (89.4% overall, Payments 89.6%, abandons 1.9%, rest of day 92.1%) but costs INR 945 and uses the last of the overtime budget, leaving nothing for later surprises.","P2 gets Payments to 88.0% and abandons to 2.1% for INR 537, but it cancels coaching. P4 (INR 312) barely improves on doing nothing.","Doing nothing also meets target, but Payments would sit lower at 84.7%."],"watch":"Watch Payments service level and General as the 2 agents leave (14:15-15:30), and look for any further absences. If either queue trends toward 80%, consider P3's overtime, which would use the last of the overtime budget."}
